title_as_printed: The dissolution enthalpy of Na2SO4 in water at 44.3 C: n1/k = n1/(nw Mw), Mw = 0.0180153 kg mol-1 and dH^ = dHexp/k = dHexp/(nw Mw)
pressure_note: not stated (no pressure printed; calorimeter cells, presumably ambient)

value.what: integral dissolution enthalpy per mole of Na2SO4 = dHexp/n1 (authors' Eq. 7); solid Na2SO4 dissolved in nw moles of water

value2.what: measured enthalpy change of the cell contents (raw calorimeter result, whole sample)

value3.what: dH^ = dHexp/(nw Mw), per kg of water

composition.other_species: solid Na2SO4 (anhydrous, Aldrich reagent grade, dried at 110 C) dissolved in twice distilled water; final molality n1/k (calculated by authors from n1 and nw)

skip_rows.reason: n1/k above the solubility limit at 44.3 C (Fig. 4 plateau, p.47): the final state is a saturated solution plus solid phase (p.44), so n1/k is not the solution molality; printed row kept in the CSV

extra_unmapped: n1 x 10^3 mol (moles of Na2SO4; scale 1e-3)
conversion_needs: molality n1/k is the molality of the final solution only if all salt dissolved (n1/k <= saturation, ~3.64 at 24.4 C, ~3.57 at 27.5 C); above that the final state is saturated solution plus solid
notes: Dissolution of solid salt into water, i.e. integral enthalpy of solution of Na2SO4 (not a gas). Rows with n1/k above the solubility limit give a plateau and are kept. Authors state nominal temperatures 24.4, 27.5, 44.3 C in text, title of paper says 25, 27.5, 45 C; Table 4 uses 297.55, 300.35, 317.45 K.
quality_remarks: Rows above the solubility limit are skipped (see skip_rows). Row 10 (n1/k 3.3422) lies at the knee of the plateau and is kept.
